subject: [PATCH v1 0/3] mm: read root memcg stats from global counters instead of flushing

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Reviewer Yosry Ahmed suggested moving the logic to read global counters directly in lruvec_page_state() and lruvec_page_state_monotonic(), as these functions already fallback to node stats when memcg is disabled, and asked if there are cases where using node stats would be incorrect.
reviews.raw_body:
Why not do this directly in lruvec_page_state() and
lruvec_page_state_monotonic()? They already fallback to node stats if
memcg is disabled, why not do the same for the root? Are there cases
where the node stats are not the right thing to do?

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that there are cases where node counters and root memcg stats may not be equal, specifically for slab's NR_SLAB_RECLAIMABLE_B and NR_SLAB_UNRECLAIMABLE_B statistics, due to the way memory is accounted in account_slab() and memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook().
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Yosry,

Thanks for taking a look at this series! I don't think we're able to
do this directly in lruvec_page_state()/lruvec_page_state_monotonic()
because I think there's still some places where the node stat and the
root memcg stat are not guaranteed to be equal.

The stat I was looking at last week was slab's NR_SLAB_RECLAIMABLE_B
and NR_SLAB_UNRECLAIMABLE_B where for those, the node counter value
can contain memory/stats that wasn't actually charged to any memcg,
which I think means for these cases, the node counter values can be
larger than what reading the root memcg rstat value would give. The
functions I was looking at were account_slab() and
memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook() where the logic adds every new slab page
to the node counter but the memcg stats only get updated if specific
criteria are met (eg the cache had SLAB_ACCOUNT set or the allocation
had the __GFP_ACCOUNT gfp flag set and the allocation was not from a
root memcg).

Thanks,
Joanne

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested special casing slab stats to avoid flushing and instead read from global counters, which aligns with the patch's goal of reducing flush overhead for root memcg
sentiment_signals: default behavior should be reading node stats without flushing
reviews.raw_body:
If it's only the slab stats, it probably makes sense to special case
those instead of the rest of the readers, right? It would be nice if
the default behavior is reading the node stats that doesn't require a
flush.

reviews.author: SJ Park
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch description does not clearly explain why some root flushes remain and requested more context on how these cases will be addressed in a subsequent patchset.

reviews.author: SJ Park
reviews.summary:
Reviewer SJ Park pointed out that the patch does not handle the case where the root memcg is not the first cgroup in the hierarchy, and suggested adding a check to ensure that the global counters are used only when the root memcg is at the top of the hierarchy.

Reviewer SJ Park noted that damos_get_node_memcg_used_bp() is called infrequently, typically only once per second, and suggested that this rate limiting already mitigates the need for global counters in this case, but acknowledged that short intervals could still cause issues

Reviewer noted that users may use DAMOS_QUOTA_NODE_MEM_{USED,FREE}_BP instead of DAMOS_QUOTA_NODE_MEMCG_{USED,FREE}_BP for root memcg, and suggested considering this when making changes

Reviewer noted that if the discussion on patch 2 concludes to have lruvec_lru_page_state(), they will provide a Reviewed-by tag.
sentiment_signals: patch does not handle edge case
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,


On Mon,  2 Nov 2026 14:50:30 -0800 Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com> wrote:

---

Just thinking loudly.  damos_get_node_memcg_used_bp() is called only once per
DAMOS quota reset interval.  It is usually recommended to set the interval to 1
second.  So a sort of rate limiting is applied in common use cases.  That said,
some users might using quite short interval.  And it is obviously better to
avoid unnecessary flushes.

---

Again, loud thought.  For root memcg, users might use
DAMOS_QUOTA_NODE_MEM_{USED,FREE}_BP instead, which calls
damos_get_node_mem_bp().  That said, some users might use
DAMOS_QUOTA_NODE_MEMCG_{USED,FREE}_BP for root memcg (maybe it makes user space
tool writing easier?).

So, looks all good to me, thank you for this patch.

---

Assuming the discussion on patch 2 concludes to have lruvec_lru_page_state(),

Reviewed-by: SJ Park <sj@kernel.org>


Thanks,
SJ

[...]

2026-11-02.patch_summary: This patch series addresses the issue of memcg stats flushing, which can be costly and introduce staleness in statistics. For the root memcg, it's possible to directly read global counters instead of going through rstat, as they are always up-to-date. The patches modify various call sites to use node counters for reading LRU sizes, working set, rotation, and reclaim writeback counts. This approach reduces the number of flushes required, especially for the root memcg, which can be a performance bottleneck. The changes also improve the accuracy of statistics by reducing staleness. The series consists of three patches: one fixes the zswap shrinker's count for the root memcg, another adds a function to read node counters for the root memcg, and the third modifies DAMON's quota goals to use node counters instead of flushing.
